review_type: single AI curator; full received final answer read; model identity visible

errors.quote: somatic targeting (O2) additionally guarantees the animal's P→other projection is untouched
errors.issue: False: Q-projecting neurons can collateralize. Somatic inhibition suppresses their other outputs too. The recommendation explicitly rejects the more appropriate local terminal test on this incorrect premise.

errors.quote: because P→other neurons are unopsined in the P→Q group
errors.issue: The packet does not establish disjoint projection populations. The different-target control cannot guarantee that the manipulated neurons or their outputs are separate.

errors.quote: a behavioral probe such as light-induced interruption of an ongoing action
errors.issue: A behavioral impairment does not independently verify neural inhibition or its kinetics; it is compatible with sensory distraction, excitation or other effects. Require appropriate physiological validation.

errors.quote: require that light-on and light-off trials within each animal be compared with locomotion as a time-varying covariate
errors.issue: Conditioning on treatment-affected locomotion can remove mediated effects or introduce selection bias. Survival or loss of the adjusted effect cannot establish retrieval specificity.

errors.quote: Opsin-negative group shows no significant light-on effect on correctness, omissions, or speed (visible-light confound controlled).
errors.issue: Nonsignificance does not exclude a meaningful light effect. Specify scientifically justified equivalence bounds and precision rather than habituating until tests become null.

errors.quote: If P→other group shows the same deficit → effect is projection-unspecific; conclusion of P→Q necessity is **not** warranted.
errors.issue: Both pathways may be necessary, or the populations may overlap. A second effective perturbation does not by itself invalidate the first pathway contribution; it undermines a uniqueness claim.

errors.quote: Power the within-subject contrast on the number of light-on vs. light-off trials per animal
errors.issue: The stated animal-level inference still needs a number-of-animals calculation using between-animal variability; trial-count precision alone cannot power the population interaction.

rationale: Includes relevant control groups, detailed behavior logging and blinded hierarchical analysis. Nevertheless, the core somatic-specificity guarantee is incorrect, validation can be circular, and movement/null-test decision rules are invalid. These prevent the claimed pathway-retrieval conclusion.
reference_guardrails: O1 establishes that population P has two targets, not that every Q-projecting neuron collateralizes. Do not assume either overlap or disjointness; validate or retain the limitation.

Projection-defined somatic inhibition tests a population and all its affected outputs. Local Q-terminal intervention is preferable for a pathway claim but also needs actual transmission and off-target validation.
Suppression in neuronal somata does not guarantee suppression of terminal transmission. Validate physiological onset, sustained effect, offset recovery and rebound at the actual behavioral settings.

Reduced normal performance supports a conditional causal requirement, not memory storage or an exclusive retrieval computation. Cue perception, attention, maintenance and motor preparation remain alternatives.
Light offset is not necessarily inhibition offset. A choice made after light ends can correctly report an earlier retrieval deficit; outcome timing alone is not a rebound diagnosis.
Movement adjustment/matching after intervention and conditioning on response completion can bias inference. Report all randomized trials and use experimental motor/sensory dissociations.
A nonsignificant control effect is not equivalence. Predefine biologically meaningful bounds and obtain enough precision to exclude consequential confounds.
Two pathways or epochs can both be necessary. Effects in an other-projection control do not by themselves invalidate the tested pathway contribution.

Numbers missing from the packet may be proposed as pilot settings; no specific opsin, surgical coordinate or animal count is mandatory. Operational calibration and justified independent-animal sampling are required.

Reference correction: population-level divergence must not be described as demonstrated single-neuron collateralization. Terminal effects on intended local Q signaling are part of the intervention, not automatically an off-target artifact.

review_sources.title: Mahn et al. (2016): biophysical constraints of presynaptic optogenetic inhibition
review_sources.scope: Reviewer-only primary-source check of terminal efficacy, paradoxical release and offset rebound; no particular construct is required by the question.
